body.statement: In the independent two-score switch experiment, the explicitly defined Gaussian donor-face benchmark \(K_{\max,\alpha,\Delta}\) satisfies \(\min_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}\Pr_{\ell}\{\ell\Delta\in K_{\max,\alpha,\Delta}(Z^{\mathrm{sw}})\}\ge1-\alpha\). Its worst-state expected diameter is \(r_{\max}(c,\Delta,\alpha)=\Delta(2\Phi(k_{\alpha})-1)[\Phi(k_{\alpha}-c)-\Phi(-k_{\alpha}-c)]\), where \((2\Phi(k_{\alpha})-1)^2=1-\alpha\). At \(\alpha=0.05\), \(c=1\), and \(\Delta=0.4\), \(r_2=0.2165\) whereas \(r_{\max}=0.3475\), so the Gaussian maximum benchmark is not minimax. Under the state-invariant independent \(U^{\mathrm{sw}}\) factorization in def:two-donor-switch, the same benchmark and risk embed in the full panel Gaussian observation.
body.justification: The proposition executes the early kill test with a fully specified score-only confidence kernel and rules out its minimax optimality.
body.gap: Berk et al. emphasize the insurance cost of simultaneity qualitatively; this calculation gives the exact cost in the donor-switch experiment.
body.consumer: It tells method developers how much expected diameter remains available to a face-adaptive replacement.
